label: Pooled sconv tails
mechanism: all four sconv sites roll their window-4 tails as one pooled gather+cat+conv per site instead of B per-row ring chains
hypothesis: Attack #3 from the exp-0005 profile, explicitly deferred by exp-0007 ('sconv remains the per-row residual'): after the pooled attention core, the four sconv sites are the largest per-row Python residual in the dispatch-bound decode step — sconv_decode_batch still steps B separate ring objects per call (B cat + B tail-copy eager launches x 4 sites x 66 layers, the copy_/cat storm exp-0005 counted: sconv = 221 ms host-side of the B=64 step, 264 call-sites), while exp-0007's measured step is 485.4 ms with sconv per-row still inside it. Pooling the tails into a per-layer-site [max_batch, k-1, C] tensor (kv.SconvPool; SconvRing rows become views, per-seq prefill seed/step bitwise-unchanged) collapses each site to ONE gather + ONE cat + ONE conv + ONE index_put_ — deleting ~90% of sconv's host enqueue from a host-enqueue-bound step. Unlike exp-0007's attention change this is BITWISE-equal to the replaced code: the same-value [B, k, C] window feeds the identical F.conv1d + fp32 residual (CPU A/B all arms torch.equal, /workspace/logs/t_sconv_pool_exp0008_2026-07-30.log).
predicted_delta: +9-18% timeboxed decode_heavy tok/s (43.3 -> ~47-51; exp-0007's bench model tok_s = 128/((128/64)*step_s + 1.93) reproduces its accepted 43.3 at step 0.485 s; deleting 180-200 ms of exp-0005's measured 221 ms sconv host time gives step ~0.285-0.31 s -> 50-51; floor assumes only half deletes under enqueue overlap -> 47)
